subject: ISV connector: publisher licensing & weights access coordination
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <alicia@openpublish.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Chris Taylor <chris@isvpartner.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 08:42:00 -0800
Subject: Publisher side: weights access & ISV bundling proposal

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the intro call last week — OpenPublish is excited about the ISV connector idea and the potential to package curated model bundles into partner marketplaces. Attached is our licensing draft (v2) and a short tech spec for the connector. High-level asks from our side:

- Limited redistribution: weights may be redistributed to certified partners for bundled/offline installs, but only under defined embargo windows and with attribution.
- Quantization/derivative artifacts allowed for performance, but original weights must be retained in escrow for audit.
- Regional restrictions: some datasets used in training mandate EU-only distribution for certain weights.
- Revenue share: 70/30 publisher/isv on bundled sales, with a 90-day review clause.

Can your legal/partner ops review and let us know must-haves vs negotiables? Chris (cc) will run the ISV packaging requirements.

Best,
Alicia
Alicia Gomez
Head of Partnerships, OpenPublish
Attachments: openpublish-licensing-draft-v2.pdf (pdf), isv-connector-tech-specs.zip (zip)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Publisher side: weights access & ISV bundling proposal

Alicia — thanks for the documents, very helpful. Quick read and initial flags from our side:

- Embargo model: we can support time-windowed embargoes but need explicit rollback/fallback policy if a partner breaches terms.
- Escrow: Ops will need a clear custody model (who holds escrow? what triggers auditor access?).
- Regional gates: we can enforce region-based distribution at the routing level, but we need the precise per-weight geography metadata.
- Commercials: we typically require a minimum annual commitment for bundled redistribution at this revenue split; can you confirm expected volume?

Looping in Vanessa and Sergio to cover legal and partner ops. Action items: Vanessa to comment on core licensing redlines, Sergio to validate operational feasibility, Chris to share ISV packaging timeline.

Thanks — Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Alliances, Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Publisher side: weights access & ISV bundling proposal

Hi Alicia — quick legal read attached (summary below). I also copied Camila for publisher program governance review.

Summary of proposed redlines (high level):
- Stronger breach & remedy clause: propose a 30-day cure period + temporary suspension before termination.
- Escrow: acceptable but must be with an industry escrow custodian; require immutable audit logs and SOC 2 Type II attestation covering the escrow process.
- Attribution: require publisher name & model id in any bundled package AND UI-level attribution in the ISV console.
- Quantization: allowed but forbid creation of weighted derivative models that are then re-published under different labels without publisher consent.

Two negotiable items: revenue share split (we can be flexible based on commit) and regional controls (technical enforcement is fine, but contract needs explicit per-asset metadata).

I'll attach redline markup by EOD.

- Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachments: vanessa-redlines-openpublish.docx (docx)

Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 14:45:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Publisher side: weights access & ISV bundling proposal

Forwarding Vanessa's note + operational checklist.

Operational checklist (items for partner/onboarding team):
1) Per-weight metadata fields added to publisher manifests: region, dataset-constraints, escrow-id, allowed-transformations.
2) Connector packaging requirements: signed manifest, integrity hash, license file.
3) Certification path for ISVs: sandbox verification (30 days) -> production enablement -> quarterly compliance attestations.
4) Distribution telemetry: tokenized usage, per-route billing, and attribution flags so we can report revenue share.

Risk callouts: offline redistribution increases entropic compliance burden (we should prefer hosted or limited-snapshot delivery where possible).

Next steps: Sergio to estimate ops effort and timelines; Karthik to propose commercial guardrails (minimum commit).

— Camila Reyes
Partner Programs, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Dana Lee <dana.lee@publaw.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 11:00:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Publisher side: weights access & ISV bundling proposal — proposed next steps

Alicia / Chris — thanks all for fast reviews and the redlines. To keep momentum, proposed next steps: 

1) Vanessa & Dana (pub legal) to align on final contract template by 2026-11-18.
2) Sergio to provide ops cost / delivery timeline for escrow + connector enforcement (ETA: 2026-11-22).
3) OpenPublish to provide per-weight metadata spreadsheet and expected monthly bundle volume by 2026-11-15.
4) Commercials: propose a 12-month minimum commitment at the 70/30 split or provide counter with expected ARR.

We prefer a design that defaults to hosted delivery (Redwood-hosted) with an opt-in limited redistribution clause for certified ISVs — this reduces compliance lift on both sides. If OpenPublish needs broader redistribution, we'll scope additional controls (extra license fee + commensurate audit rights).

Please reply-all with confirmations or adjustments. If we can lock legal and the metadata sheet this week, we can align engineering for a Jan '27 pilot.

Thanks — Karthik
Head of Alliances, Redwood Inference
